- When sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent dip, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at +10% above prior peak to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is falling, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast over 5+ days, apply a 1–3% downward bias correction for next 7-day horizon.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed and forecast is volatile, smooth out 3–5 day moving average to reduce noise.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome is below 10% of forecast range, assume mean reversion and adjust downward by 1–2% per week.
